# story-long-scan: Chinese web-novel market rank scanning (Qidian, Fanqie, Jinjiang…)

Curated by Skill Harbor — @zenstory-ai's story-long-scan: a long-form web-novel market analyst for the Chinese platforms (Qidian, Fanqie, Jinjiang, Qimao, Ciweimao). It runs a five-phase pipeline — confirm platform and direction, acquire real ranking data (script scraping first, user-supplied second, built-in knowledge last), analyze genre distribution/word-count/title patterns/new-element signals, output a structured market report (genre heat ranking, new-genre signals, classic-genre dynamics, word-count medians, tag buzzwords, worth-watching directions), and turn findings into topic decisions with hard feasibility rules (sparse data caps feasibility at "medium"). Core belief: one ranking is a clue, only repeated cross-sample patterns are a signal. MIT-licensed. Honest notes: the entire skill is written in Chinese and targets Chinese platforms — irrelevant if you don't write for that market; ranking data goes stale fast, and built-in-knowledge mode must be labeled as hypothesis-only until re-scanned. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
